summary: 3D ray-sphere collision routine with sliding response. Computes a vector from the ray point advanced by a3 along direction a2 to the sphere center a4, scaled by coefficient dword_5D3488. If the squared length of that vector is below threshold flt_5D348C, computes the ray-sphere intersection distance (sqrt of a discriminant minus a dot-product term) and, when it is positive, slides the ray origin a1 forward to the contact point by t_hit * a2. Operates on float triplets; returns void.

operations.description: Scale direction components a2[1] and a2[2] by coefficient dword_5D3488 and subtract from sphere center a4 to form part of the relative vector.
Build relative vector v12/v14/v17 = advanced ray point (a1 moved by a3 * a2) minus the scaled sphere center a4.
If squared length of the relative vector (v17*v17 + v14*v14 + v12*v12) is not below flt_5D348C, skip the intersection test.
Compute t = dot(relative vector, direction a2).
Compute discriminant v7 = flt_5D348C - squared perpendicular distance from the sphere center to the ray.
If discriminant v7 is not greater than 0.0, the ray misses the sphere; skip the slide.
Compute intersection distance t_hit = sqrt(discriminant) - t.
If t_hit is not greater than 0.0, the intersection lies behind the ray origin; skip the slide.
Slide ray origin a1 to the contact point: a1[0..2] += t_hit * a2[0..2], updating offsets 0x0, 0x4 and 0x8.
